This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day, The
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ashok S. Kinagi)
1.

This Appeal is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 25.08.2020 passed in MVC No.1127/2017 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Saundatti (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal').
2. Brief facts, leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
3. On 16.01.2017, the deceased Fakirappa Laxman Godi along with his friend Sanjeev Fakkirappa were returning from Munavalli to Chunchanur on a motorcycle bearing registration No.K23/EC-8944.

entities.text: Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Saundatti
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: When they were near Munvalli-Kadakol road, at that time a tractor and trailer bearing registration NC: 2026:KHC-D:3636 HC-KAR No.AP-02/W-6521 and trailer bearing No.KA-24/TA-6801 came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Motorcycle.
As a result, deceased Fakirappa sustained a grievous injury, and later on succumbed to the injuries.
The legal representatives of the deceased Fakirapppa filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act seeking compensation on account of death of the deceased Fakirappa.

Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
4. Respondent No.1, the owner of the tractor appeared through the counsel, however he did not choose to file a statement of objections.

5. The Insurance Company filed a statement of objections, denying the averments made in the claim petition and contented that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle, and that the driver of the tractor was not holding the valid and effective driving The Divisional Manager vs Laxman S/O. Fakirappa Godi on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145995621/
2 license as on the date of the accident.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Laxman S/O. Fakirappa Godi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petition against the respondent No.2-the Insurance Company.
6. The Tribunal, based on the rival pleadings of the parties framed the relevant issues.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3636 HC-KAR 7.
The petitioner/claimants to substantiate their case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1 and marked 27 documents as Exs.P1 to P27.
In rebuttal, the Insurance Company examined its officer as RW-1 and marked four documents as Ex.R5 to R8.
As far as Exs.R1 to R4 are concerned, they were marked with the consent from the petitioners.

8. The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence allowed the claim petition in part with costs vide Judgment dated 25.08.2020 and awarded a compensation of 12,24,000/- and held that the respondent No.2-Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation.
9. The Insurance Company, aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, filed this Miscellaneous First Appeal.

10. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company and the learned counsel for the claimants.
11.
Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that the deceased was aged about 17 years and he was a bachelor.
The Tribunal, instead of deducting 50% towards the personal expenses of the deceased Fakirappa, has deducted one NC: 2026:KHC-D:3636 HC-KAR third which is incorrect.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.
12. Per contra, learned for the claimants supported the impugned judgment and accordingly prays to dismiss the appeal.

13. Perused, the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
14.
The point that would arise for consideration is regarding to the quantum of compensation.

15. It is an undisputed fact that the deceased Fakirappa met with an accident and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the tractor and the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the tractor.
The Tribunal was justified in recording the finding that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor.
Regarding quantum of compensation 16.
The petitioners contend that the deceased Fakirappa was aged about 17 years and the accident is of 2017.
He was studying in the SSLC and he was very active in the education.
The petitioners to substantiate the case, they have not produced any records to show the income proof.

sentences.text: This Court assesses the notional income at 10,250/-.
The deceased was aged about 17 years and the accident is of 2017.
The income of the deceased is taken at 10,250/- as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

18. In addition to it, in view of the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% future prospect is to be added, which comes to 10,250/- + 4,100/- =
14,350/-.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was bachelor, therefore, 50% is to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased i.e. 14,350/-  2 = 7,175/-.

The multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is '18'.
19.
Thus, the petitioners are entitled to a compensation of 15,49,800/- (7,175/- x 12 x 18).

In addition to it, there are two petitioners, each petitioner is entitled for consortium i.e. 48,000/- x 2 = 96,000/- and in addition to it, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the heads of loss of estate 18,000/- and funeral expenses 18,000/-.
Thus the petitioners are entitled to a total compensation of 16,81,800/-.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3636 HC-KAR 20.
Admittedly, in the instant case the petitioners have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
I do not find any grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that the petitioners are satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
21. In view of the above circumstances, I do not find any grounds to entertain the appeal.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is dismissed.
(ii) The amount in deposit and the trial Court records, if any shall be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned, forthwith.
Sd/-
